narrative.overview:
Lembrion is set like a well-made Metropolis Beamer deck. One dark teal title bar carries the wordmark and the routes; below it sits a pale ground with one idea per frame, and during a session a 4px progress line under the bar records every answer. Hierarchy comes from type size and weight and from rules (a 2px ink rule under each section title, hairlines between rows), not from boxes. Explanation and feedback arrive in titled blocks: a teal title strip over a pale teal-grey body, exactly as Metropolis draws them.

The density is that of a good handout: counts live in data tables and facts lists with right-aligned tabular figures, controls state their exact values, and the right column of a two-column frame holds the facts of the current session or the next action. Colour is disciplined. Teal does the structural work (title bar, primary buttons, block titles, heading rules); Metropolis orange marks only where the learner is (progress, the current item, the active route, reviews due); green and red appear only to report state. Three themes (light, dark, contrast) share one set of token names, so every component follows the active theme without a reload.

The world is flat. PRODUCT.md binds it to no skeuomorphism, and the shipped build carries no gradients, glow, icon tiles, or stacked shadowed cards; the only shadow in the system belongs to things that float (the theme menu, dialogs and toasts).
keyCharacteristics: A single dark teal title bar, sticky, 3.5rem tall, white Fira Sans on teal.
One orange rule: the progress line, the loading line, and the 3px underline under the active route or tab.
Titled blocks (teal strip, pale teal-grey body) for every explanation and piece of feedback.
Tables and facts lists with tabular figures right-aligned; no stat tiles.
Two radii only (2px and 4px); 1px borders; 2px ink rules under section titles.
Flat content on a tonal ground; shadows only on overlays.
Fira Sans for everything, Fira Mono for keys, model IDs, URLs and code; sentence-case copy.

rules.name: The Where-You-Are Rule
rules.body: Orange marks progress and the current item only: the current progress segment, the loading line, the active route and tab underline, review boxes with questions due, and "Active" or due labels. It never fills a button, a heading, a block, or a decorative surface.

rules.name: The Ink Twin Rule
rules.body: Every signal hue has an ink twin. The base (accent, success, error, warning) fills rules, strips and tints; text in that hue always uses the `*Ink` token. Light-theme Metropolis Orange is 2.62:1 on the ground and never carries text.

rules.name: The Tint, Not Fill Rule
rules.body: State surfaces are tints mixed into the surface with `color-mix(in srgb, <hue> N%, var(--color-surface))`, never solid fills: choice checked (primary 8%), option selected (primary 9%), option correct (success 12%), option wrong (error 10%), success block body (success 10%), error block body (error 9%), error notice (error 10%), warning notice (warning 14%), accent tag (accent 16%), success tag (success 14%), error tag (error 12%), danger button hover (error 10%). The only solid state fills are block title strips and progress segments.

rules.name: The Size-and-Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is size and weight (400, 500, 600) plus rules. No text is uppercased or letter-spaced anywhere; tracking moves only on the page title (-0.01em) and the wordmark (0.01em). No kickers or eyebrows above titles.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every count, score, percentage, ratio and date sets in tabular figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) and right-aligns in table number columns and facts values. Ratios are written with spaced slashes ("3 / 5", "0 / 1"); topic lists join with " · ".

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All UI copy is sentence case: "Start review", "Recent sessions", "New study session", "End session".

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text never runs wider than 68ch. Wide content (tables, two-column frames) may use the full 72rem; prose may not.

rules.name: The Overlays-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this floats above the page". Tables, blocks, choice groups, option rows and every other piece of content sit flat on the ground; if it does not float, it does not cast.

rules.name: The Two Radii Rule
rules.body: 2px for what you read, 4px for what you press or type into; nothing rounder.

dos: Do put every route inside the 72rem frame under the teal title bar, open with one `page-title`, and head each section with a `section-title` and its 2px ink rule.
Do give each screen one primary (Deck Teal) button for the next step; make every other action secondary or ghost.
Do keep Metropolis Orange for progress and the current item, and set orange text in Burnt Orange Ink.
Do set counts, scores, ratios and dates in tabular figures, right-aligned in tables and facts lists.
Do put explanations and feedback in titled blocks, and show grading as a tint mixed into the surface plus inked text.

Do style through the semantic tokens (`bg-shell`, `text-ink-soft`, `border-line-strong`) so all three themes follow; build tints with `color-mix()` in CSS, because the token classes take no `/opacity` modifier.
Do show any AI wait as the 4px loading rule with a one-line label.
Do raise transient, out-of-flow messages through the toast: a surface panel with a 4px state rule on top, a title and a short message.
Do write UI copy in sentence case.
donts: Don't use skeuomorphic texture, gradients or glow; PRODUCT.md rules out skeuomorphism.
Don't put a shadow on content; only menus, dialogs and toasts carry the overlay shadow.
Don't build stat tiles, icon tiles or stacked shadowed cards; numbers belong in data tables and facts lists.
Don't add a coloured side stripe to notices or blocks; state is a tint plus inked text.
Don't fill buttons, headings or surfaces with orange, or set text in the base accent.
Don't uppercase or letter-space labels, or put kickers or eyebrows above titles.
Don't round anything past 4px or draw pills.
Don't hard-code hex in components; every colour comes from a `--color-*` token so the three themes stay whole.
